instrumentTitle: Portland City Charter, Article 1 The Council

regions.beginsWith: The City Council of the City of Portland consists of twelve (12) Councilors. There are four (4) City Council districts. Each district is represented by three (3) Councilors. The Mayor is not a member of Council.
regions.endsWith: The City Council of the City of Portland consists of twelve (12) Councilors. There are four (4) City Council districts. Each district is represented by three (3) Councilors. The Mayor is not a member of Council.

regions.beginsWith: All regular and special meetings of the Council shall be public. The Council meets the first week of January following each general election and thereafter meets at the time and place fixed by ordinance. The Council shall keep a journal of its proceedings which shall be a public record.
regions.endsWith: All regular and special meetings of the Council shall be public. The Council meets the first week of January following each general election and thereafter meets at the time and place fixed by ordinance. The Council shall keep a journal of its proceedings which shall be a public record.

regions.beginsWith: At any meeting of the Council seven (7) Councilors constitute a quorum, but a lesser number may adjourn or recess from time to time, and may compel the attendance of absent members.
regions.endsWith: At any meeting of the Council seven (7) Councilors constitute a quorum, but a lesser number may adjourn or recess from time to time, and may compel the attendance of absent members.

instrumentTitle: Portland City Charter, Section 1-101 corporate identity

regions.beginsWith: The municipal corporation now existing and known as the City of Portland shall remain and continue a body politic and corporate by the name of the City of Portland,
regions.endsWith: The municipal corporation now existing and known as the City of Portland shall remain and continue a body politic and corporate by the name of the City of Portland,

instrumentTitle: Portland City Charter, Section 2-101 Municipal Powers Allocation

regions.beginsWith: The municipal powers and authority of the City are vested as follows: legislative and quasi-judicial authority is vested in the City Council and executive and administrative authority is vested in the Mayor, subject to the initiative and referendum and other powers reserved to the people by the constitution of the State of Oregon as defined and prescribed by the provisions of the constitution and general laws relating thereto, and by any more specific allocation set forth in this Charter.
regions.endsWith: The municipal powers and authority of the City are vested as follows: legislative and quasi-judicial authority is vested in the City Council and executive and administrative authority is vested in the Mayor, subject to the initiative and referendum and other powers reserved to the people by the constitution of the State of Oregon as defined and prescribed by the provisions of the constitution and general laws relating thereto, and by any more specific allocation set forth in this Charter.

regions.beginsWith: At its first regular meeting each calendar year, or oftener at its option, the Council shall elect a President and Vice President by majority vote of those present. The President shall preside at all meetings of the Council. In the President's absence or incapacity, the Vice President of the Council shall perform the duties of the President.
regions.endsWith: At its first regular meeting each calendar year, or oftener at its option, the Council shall elect a President and Vice President by majority vote of those present. The President shall preside at all meetings of the Council. In the President's absence or incapacity, the Vice President of the Council shall perform the duties of the President.
